Under the split-extension reading this is false, even for a degree-one line bundle on a complex elliptic curve. mu_n: For a P^1 boundary with normal-bundle degree d, the tame inertia predicted by the homotopy sequence is coker(d:T^(p-prime)→T^(p-prime)). It is cyclic of order |d| with its p-part removed when d≠0; for d=0 it is the whole Tate module.

title: Arithmetic finiteness, nonabelianity, and the infinite place
as_he_states: sans doute: An apparent blanket assertion that the arithmetic tame fundamental group is abelian or finite is reading-dependent; the abelianization formula and infinity-place convention must be separated.

title: From the finite-coefficient H² functor to pi₂

title: Does uniqueness of the infinitesimal kernel require reducedness?

title: Complete the monic-factor argument

title: Local and global Bertini variants
as_he_states: Théorème de Bertini et variantes: Let f:X→P^r_k with X a geometrically irreducible algebraic k-scheme and n=dim closure(f(X)). For a generic linear subspace of codimension s≤n−1, the inverse section is geometrically irreducible. Théorème de Bertini et variantes: If the image of the locus where f is ramified or X fails the selected unibranch/normal/smooth property has dimension<s, a generic codimension-s linear inverse section has the selected property. Théorème de Bertini et variantes: Over algebraically closed k the indicated generic section surjects on pi1(X); after extension to the geometric generic parameter the full pi1 comparison requires properness, while the prime-to-characteristic quotient has a broader version. Théorème de Bertini et variantes: If X is proper and geometrically irreducible, every linear inverse section in the stated codimension range is geometrically connected; with the local hypotheses the induced pi1 map is surjective.
plausible_today: Keep geometric irreducibility, image-dimension bounds, local normal/unibranch/smooth conditions, properness and base-field extension separate. A Grassmannian incidence argument handles connected special sections; arbitrary special sections cannot simply be iterated as irreducible ones.
state_of_art: CL-SA12-240: As of 2026-11-19: The general geometric-irreducibility assertion is established. Poonen–Slavov Theorem1.8 and §7 prove that the bad hyperplanes are a finite exceptional-image union plus a constructible set of dimension≤codim(image)+1; when image dimension≥2 this is a proper subset of the dual projective space. This covers arbitrary morphisms of geometrically irreducible finite-type varieties, without properness or normality. Generic successive sections give the stated higher-codimension range. SGA1X2.10 invokes Bertini under its proper/normal hypotheses; the exact broader development is classified B rather than silently assigned to that narrower printed invocation. The paper traces the earlier theorem to Jouanolou1983 Theorem6.3(4), whose text was not opened here. CL-SA12-241: As of 2026-11-19: The opened EGA IV4 and SGA1 passages establish the local unramified/smooth machinery and the global irreducibility argument. Avoidance of a locus with image dimension<s is immediate for a generic codimension-s linear section. However, the exact combined unibranch/normal/smooth formulation has not been identified with one unchanged printed theorem; its local-property clauses and field-extension hypotheses remain separated. This is a partial precise match, not an assertion that every clause is still open. CL-SA12-242: As of 2026-11-19: SGA1 X1.8 verifies proper base-field invariance and X2.10–2.11 the section-surjectivity mechanism. X1.10 explicitly gives characteristic-p failures without properness. The page itself refuses to assert full nonproper base-changed surjectivity; the earlier notes should not erase this limitation. CL-SA12-243: As of 2026-11-19: SGA1 X2.10–2.11 proves the hyperplane version by generic Bertini and Zariski connectedness. For higher codimension, the reconstruction uses the universal Grassmannian incidence family, whose total space and geometric generic fibre are irreducible. Properness and Stein connectedness over the normal Grassmannian give geometrically connected special fibres. Applying this to connected finite étale covers requires the stated geometric-unibranch/local hypotheses. Merely iterating a special-hyperplane theorem would be insufficient because an intermediate special section need not be irreducible; no such iteration is used here.
why_open: The pages list variants with brief reasons and cross-references; an exact unchanged printed home for the entire local-property list was not established.
worth: Worth a theorem concordance with all quantifiers; this is a better bounded task than a general new Bertini theorem.

title: Tame Lefschetz with a boundary
as_he_states: Cet homomorphisme est surjectif: With X proper, Y=f^−1(L) nonempty and smooth of codimension s along Y, f unramified there, and the boundary near Y either codimension≥2 or a divisor inducing normal crossings on Y, restriction from U=X−D to U∩Y induces a surjection on the specified tame fundamental groups.
plausible_today: For regular proper pairs with strict normal crossings, use Esnault–Kindler Theorem1.1: Lef gives surjectivity, Leff plus meeting effective divisors gives isomorphism. Retain the draft’s own codimension/transversality conditions when comparing.
state_of_art: CL-SA12-244: As of 2026-11-19: SGA7 XVIII6.1 is the published tame-surjectivity argument using SGA1 XIII specialization. Esnault–Kindler2016 Theorem1.1 gives the regular strict-normal-crossing version under Lef, and an isomorphism under Leff plus intersection of all effective divisors. Their result and §6 handle stated variants, but do not silently identify every draft boundary convention.
why_open: The draft proof refers to tame specialization and Bertini. Later formulations use explicit hypotheses, not every possible boundary convention.
worth: Worth a short comparison of the archival and modern boundary conditions; core results are established.

title: Vanishing-cycle conjugacy in characteristic two
as_he_states: j’ignore si elle reste vraie pour un pinceau général: Local vanishing cycles of a Lefschetz pencil are conjugate up to sign, and the vanishing cohomology is irreducible under the stated Lefschetz hypothesis, except that the manuscript cannot prove the characteristic2/odd-total-dimension case for a general pencil.
plausible_today: For every Lefschetz pencil on a smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed field, vanishing cycles with finite coefficients of order prime to the characteristic are conjugate up to sign; the required vanishing-cohomology hypotheses remain for irreducibility.
state_of_art: CL-SA12-245: As of 2026-11-19: The question is settled: Deligne WeilII4.2.7–4.2.8 proves the sufficiently general pencil result with Q_l coefficients; Orgogozo2005/2006 §11.2–11.4 proves conjugacy and equality of monodromy images for every Lefschetz pencil, without a transversality restriction, with Z/l^nu coefficients, l≠char(k). Illusie2006 Theorem5.2 states this explicitly and credits Gabber's image-equality argument to a letter of14March2005. Irreducibility follows with the usual vanishing-cohomology/Lefschetz assumptions; no such condition is dropped.
why_open: The manuscript expressly leaves the characteristic2/odd-total-dimension case open. Deligne1980 handles sufficiently general pencils; Orgogozo2005/2006 §11 settles all pencils, with Gabber’s2005 monodromy-image argument.
worth: Closed: retain as a strong example of a historical question whose modern answer is more complete than the original SGA account.

title: Uniform completion on the reused sheet
as_he_states: filtres de Cauchy minimaux: Minimal Cauchy filters produce the separated completion of a uniform space, with entourages constructed from pairs of filters meeting a common small set.

Searches for the exact wording have not identified the typescript edition/page. The ambient X/W symbols in the transcribed composition formula need scan inspection; the argument must concern the induced entourages on the completion.

title: The relative étale Künneth diagram
as_he_states: surjectif; isomorphisme: For X→S proper separable surjective with universally connected fibres and Y connected locally noetherian over S, pi1(X×_S Y)→pi1(X)×_pi1(S)pi1(Y) is surjective. Under the written section or finite-etale base-change/injectivity condition it is an isomorphism.

title: Finite-group quotients of nonseparated étale schemes
as_he_states: cas fini: The page proposes that a finite group action on an étale Y-scheme has an open free locus and an étale quotient, with an uncertain finite-case restriction. The finite étale version is valid; the arbitrary nonseparated version is false.
plausible_today: The finite étale version has a clopen free locus and finite étale quotient. For general nonseparated étale schemes the doubled-origin involution disproves the claimed open free locus.
state_of_art: CL-SA12-255: As of 2026-11-19: The finite-etale case is standard SGA1 V quotient theory. On the line with doubled origin over A1, the involution swapping origins is identity on the common punctured line; its free locus consists of the origins and is not open. This meets etaleness and finite-group-action hypotheses, so the tentative finite-case correction is essential.
why_open: The source has a tentative cas fini qualification. Its intended placement is mathematically decisive.
worth: Closed as a diagnostic; the next useful step is scan collation of that qualification.

title: Direct images and relative Hom of finite covers
as_he_states: conoyau fini: A proper dominant morphism X→Y with Y connected normal locally noetherian has finite-index image on etale fundamental groups. universellement ouvert: For a suitable universally open morphism, direct image of finite etale coverings should again admit an etale/finite representability description; the category and finiteness conditions are not fully fixed.

SGA1 IX descent and X proper separable cases are exact established special cases. The draft universal-open criterion was not matched to an opened theorem with all its quantifiers.

worth: Worth isolating one exact representability functor and testing its local constancy, not extrapolating from constructibility.

title: Strict prorepresentability for infinite discrete groups
as_he_states: exact à gauche: For connected S, the pointed torsor functor on discrete groups is left exact: it preserves products, injections and equalizers. minimal: Minimal reductions and surjective transitions yield strict prorepresentability of the discrete-group pointed torsor functor over connected locally noetherian S; an Artinian structural-group condition gives another minimality route.

state_of_art: CL-SA12-261: As of 2026-11-19: SGA3 X6.1–6.2 is the later framework for representable constant-group torsors. Equalizers of two pointed maps are clopen reductions; connectedness forces the reduction containing the chosen point to cover S. This is not the finite-flat S-group equalizer argument refuted in CL-SA12-223. CL-SA12-262: As of 2026-11-19: SGA3 X6.2 explicitly states strict prorepresentability for connected locally noetherian S; the corrected edition notes that one deduction can be expanded. For topological inverse limits, Bhatt–Scholze Lemma7.4.6 shows the same discrete torsor representations are recovered. The group-homomorphism statement must not be confused with the false arbitrary-Set criterion of scan183.

title: Five topology classes and effectiveness
as_he_states: effectivité: The five classes of torsors defined using the listed descent topologies should coincide for finite structural groups, with additional Dedekind and complete-local comparison claims for the infinite classes.

title: Simplicial components and finite presentation bounds

title: The three-condition Set-functor criterion
as_he_states: conditions a), b), c): The page claims that a left-exact F:Set→Set preserving filtered intersections and strictly prorepresented by (K_i), with all lim K_i→K_i surjective, equals the functor I↦C(lim K_i,I_discrete) for the ordinary inverse-limit topology. All three assumptions can hold while this equality fails.
plausible_today: The stated sufficiency criterion is false. For K_n=N^n, F(I)=colim Hom(K_n,I) is left exact and preserves intersections, all limit projections are onto, yet x↦x_(x0+1) is continuous on N^N without factoring through a fixed prefix. Uniform continuity or a finite compact system repairs this test.
state_of_art: CL-SA12-270: As of 2026-11-19: The Baire example K_i=N^i meets all three displayed assumptions, but f(x)=x_(x0+1) is continuous without factoring through one finite prefix. Thus the proposed sufficiency criterion is false. Uniform continuity to a discrete target, or a finite compact inverse system, repairs this example. Bourbaki195 warns that an ordinary inverse limit does not replace a pro-object; Bhatt–Scholze7.4.6 concerns group homomorphisms, which are uniformly continuous, and does not contradict the counterexample.
why_open: The source states three conditions but supplies no argument controlling nonuniform continuous maps. No claim is made that the author knew this counterexample.
worth: Worth a concise counterexample companion; broader repaired representability theorems are separate research tasks.

title: Limits of continuously represented functors
as_he_states: T-représentable: For an actual diagram of topological spaces K_a, the continuous-map functors I↦C(K_a,I_discrete) have pointwise limits represented by the colimit space equipped with its final topology.
plausible_today: For an actual diagram of spaces, colimits with the final topology represent the pointwise limit of continuous-map functors. For arbitrary natural transformations between such functors, full faithfulness must be justified separately.
state_of_art: CL-SA12-271: As of 2026-11-19: This follows directly from the universal property of the colimit in topological spaces: a map out is continuous exactly when all component maps are. It does not show that every natural transformation of such restricted Set-valued functors comes from a continuous map, nor does it rescue the false criterion on scan183. Bourbaki195 supplies the variance distinction for representable functors.
why_open: The sketch moves from a space diagram to a category-of-functors claim; the missing realization of arbitrary natural transformations is a distinct issue.
worth: Worth a narrowly defined categorical check after settling the precise morphisms in the manuscript’s category.

title: From groups to categories in the component construction
as_he_states: Van Kampen: A half-cosimplicial/topological pi0/pi1 formalism should extend from groups to categories at points and supply a van Kampen description.
plausible_today: The component nerve gives an established group presentation; a category-valued extension needs specified objects, morphisms, descent and equivalences.
state_of_art: CL-SA12-272: As of 2026-11-19: SGA3 X6.3 gives the component-simplicial group construction; Artin–Mazur develops a broader etale homotopy type. Localic and pro-etale work are relevant later frameworks, but the manuscript does not specify a unique higher categorical theorem. Searches found no exact match for every proposed category-valued extension; no claim of undeveloped novelty is made.
why_open: The last lines state a direction rather than a precise conjecture. No publication is treated as an exact solution solely because it concerns higher categories.
worth: Defer until a concrete statement is extracted; no open-problem novelty is asserted.

title: Finite type from finite components over a Japanese base
as_he_states: type fini: Let Y be locally noetherian and universally Japanese. A separated locally quasi-finite morphism X→Y with finitely many irreducible components is of finite type.
plausible_today: A separated locally quasi-finite morphism with finitely many irreducible components over a locally noetherian universally Japanese base is finite type. Normalize the components, use finite normalization over the base and the local birational open-immersion theorem, then descend quasi-compactness.
state_of_art: CL-SA12-273: As of 2026-11-19: The intended theorem follows from Nagata finite normalization and the normal-target birational form of Zariski's main theorem; the independent proof in §8 corrects the direction of the argument. The displayed normalization→X arrow already fails for a strict open immersion into normal Y. Stacks normalization/generically finite references verify the standard inputs; the faulty arrow is listed for scan review. Stacks37.43.2 (02LR) supplies the quasi-finite separated normalization factorization; apply it to quasi-compact local pieces before invoking the global finite-component argument, so quasi-compactness is not assumed at the step being proved.
why_open: The intended theorem has a proof, but a displayed arrow from the base normalization to X has the wrong general direction; a strict open immersion already disproves that arrow.
worth: Closed by the corrected proof; useful as a companion example of a valid theorem with an invalid proof step.

title: The anonymous local pairing fragment
as_he_states: noyau d’Albanese; j_o: The local correction symbol j_o attached to divisor/zero-cycle data on an abelian variety is symmetric after translating and moving cycles through the Albanese kernel; it vanishes in the stated identity-component situation. The fragment presupposes definitions and formulas(2),(3) on missing preceding pages.
